notes: Hook overclaimed: "A flow meter that works by pressure difference sends 12 mA" leaves out that the 12 mA is the pressure-difference cell's signal; a transmitter with square-root extraction would send 12 mA at 50% flow. Research [14] says "a 12 mA signal from the DP cell, that's 50% DP, but 71% flow rate". Corrected to "A flow meter's pressure-difference cell sends 12 mA ...". 12 mA is halfway up 4 to 20 mA (checked), and about 71% matches the square root of 0.5, 0.707 (checked).

In one breath overclaimed: "each takes only certain inputs and gives only certain outputs" is false for the line and the cube, which take every input (and the square takes every input too). Corrected to "some take only certain inputs or give only certain outputs".

In one breath: "sit behind many of the laws you use at work" claimed more than the research backs (one cited law per shape: 4 to 20 mA scaling [12], I squared R [16], propeller law [15], Boyle hyperbola [18], DP square root [13]). Narrowed to "sit behind laws you use at work".

Checked and kept: function = exactly one output per input [1]; sliding, stretching and flipping change the rule predictably [5][6][19][20]; chaining feeds one output into the next [9]; running a machine backwards as rearranging [10]. Lesson i1 agrees with the corrected overview.
